elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Rendered 15.6 retains the proviso as a PB-only carve-out: "PB may assign, sublicense or transfer this Agreement and all of its rights and obligations hereunder, in their entirety, to any of its Affiliates" — no consent required. "Affiliate" is a defined term (1.1.2).

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Same proviso continues "...or to a successor in connection with the sale or other transfer of all or substantially all of its business or assets to which this Agreement relates, whether by merger, sale of stock, sale of assets or otherwise", operating as an exception to the consent requirement.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: The proviso was narrowed from "either Party" to "PB", so the opening bar — "Without the prior written consent of the other Party hereto ... neither Party will sell, transfer, assign, pledge or otherwise dispose of ... this Agreement or any of its rights or duties hereunder" — now applies to SFJ with no carve-out.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Inserted parenthetical: "(which consent, in the case of an assignment by SFJ, will not be unreasonably withheld)".

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: Final paragraph now reads "SFJ shall not at any time sell, assign, sublicense or otherwise transfer this Agreement to an entity whose primary business is the development or commercialization of pharmaceutical or biotechnology products"; the Program Transfer sunset and the PB sole-discretion consent gate are deleted, making the bar absolute and permanent for a pharma/biotech (i.e., PB-competitor) transferee.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2.6 as rendered states "SFJ shall have no right to terminate this Agreement as a result of a Change of Control of PB"; the sole-discretion termination sentence and the 150% Development Costs consequence are deleted, and the heading is conformed to "Change of Control of PB".

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: The successor carve-out was deliberately narrowed to PB only; SFJ now needs PB's prior written consent for any transfer, including to a successor. (Consistent with the preferred target, but it fails this fallback element.)

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: No notice mechanic was added to 15.6; the only notice obligation is PB's Change of Control notice in 14.2.6, which is not an assignment-notice covenant.
PB retains a no-consent affiliate exception (a non-successor exception), which under the fallback test defeats "Other assignments require consent."

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The reasonableness standard is one-directional — it governs only "an assignment by SFJ"; consent to a PB assignment outside the carve-out remains at SFJ's unqualified discretion.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all six preferred elements are met in operative language (PB affiliate/successor carve-outs retained, SFJ consent gate with a not-unreasonably-withheld standard, permanent competitor bar, express no-termination-on-Change-of-Control statement).

Fallback is not met (mutual successor right removed, no written-notice mechanic, retained PB affiliate no-consent exception, one-way reasonableness standard), but that is irrelevant because the preferred checklist is complete.

Minimal: each edit maps to a selected element. Narrowing the proviso to PB is required for "Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent"; deleting the Program Transfer sunset and the PB sole-discretion consent gate is required to make the competitor bar "never"; deleting the 150% Development Costs payment and the termination-conditioned continuation/Approval Payment sentences avoids dangling operative text keyed to a termination right that no longer exists. No survival tails, expense language, damages categories, or unrelated boilerplate were added.

Intent preserved: PB's Change of Control notice obligation survives, Article 6 (including the Section 6.2 adjustment and the Section 6.7 Buy-Out Payment credit) continues to govern Approval Payments independently, and the deleted consequences operated only "following the date of such termination".

Verification point for the drafter (not a defect on the record provided): confirm that no other provision — in particular Section 6.2, Section 6.7 (Change of Control Buy-Out Payment) or Section 11.1.1.4 — cross-refers to "Section 14.2.6" or to termination thereunder; if any does, add a conforming reference deletion so no dangling cross-reference remains.

Note for the cover comment: the redline removes a Customer-side flexibility (PB can no longer consent to an SFJ transfer to a pharma/biotech acquirer). That is the deliberate consequence of the preferred "never assign to a competitor" position and should be flagged to the client as a trade-off.
